objective: Each Historical record card shows the record's top three, the holder's name in bold, each entry in at most two lines.
acceptance_criteria: Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation; the implementation commit edits no test. Start gate: after EVENTS-016 and FRONTEND-041 merge.

A card keeps its title (and its category line) and lists the holder's `top` entries (EVENTS-016) in order as a list. Each entry is line 1: the team icon (team records, and a player's single-game record: the team they played for), the name (a team's short name from teamShortName; a player's full name) and the value (RecordValue, as today); line 2: the season or game date in --font-size-sm and --color-text-muted.
No entry takes more than two lines at 320 px: line 1 does not wrap and is cut with an ellipsis, the full text staying in the DOM for assistive technology.

The holder's name and value are --font-weight-semibold; so is any entry tied with it (equal value: also a holder). Every other entry is regular weight. When more entries share the record than the card shows, a muted line says how many more.
Fewer than three entries shows what there is; none shows 'Nothing qualifies yet.' The loading placeholder keeps the card's final height (no layout shift when holders arrive).
On a record's own level (its ranked list), the names of rank-1 entries are semibold too.
Requests unchanged: one holders read per page of 24 cards; no per-card read.

The full frontend suite (vitest --maxWorkers=2), npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm run build pass. The bundle-budget test passes with this unit's own file in frontend/src/test/bundle-budgets/ declaring every output it changes; no other unit's file is edited.

Browser rows (FrontendUI/verification.md), Chrome, light and dark, at 320, 360, 768 and 1280 px unless a criterion names other widths: each row measured or reported NOT DONE in the PR, with no document-level horizontal overflow and no page error. Rows: Best regular season (Warriors 73-9 2015-16 first), a player single-game record, a tied record; light/dark contrast of the muted line measured.
